speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any specific triggers for your gait instability, such as worsening symptoms when looking down or when walking in the dark?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like cerebellar ataxia. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any difficulty with speech, such as slurring or a scanning pattern, or any changes in your handwriting? Also, do you have any known history of autoimmune disorders, recent infections, or significant weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (T2/FLAIR).

Given your history with Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, your right-sided ataxia and gait instability are highly concerning for PML. Do you have any new visual disturbances or changes in sensation on your right side?
